title: M-C Mega Ambiguity
lede: Salamence-centered M-C six: Mega Salamence + Primarina + Gholdengo as the default three, with Garchomp, Golisopod, and Lucario as flex Mega options. Register six → read their six → pick which stone and which support make their plan hardest.
philosophy: Teammate frequency is correlation, not a finished six. Build a preview toolbox that can produce several strong threes, not a fixed Salamence + top-five partners list. Four Mega stones create real preview pressure — you only click one.
meta: Regulation M-C (Sept 9–Dec 2, 2026) newly legalized Mega Salamence, Mega Garchomp, Mega Lucario, and Mega Golisopod (plus Mega Absol Z and Mega Baxcalibur). Only one Mega Evolution per battle. Season M-6 ladder after week one put Salamence, Garchomp, Primarina, Golisopod/Hippowdon, and Lucario at the top of Singles — an unusually clean link between the new Mega pool and usage.
setsNote: 66 SP, max 32 per stat. Four Mega stones on the six — only one Mega per battle. Default training mirrors current M-C ladder concentrations; swap natures only when Speed tiers demand it.

evidence.source: Pokémon Zone Singles ranked + Champions News M-C Mega pool
evidence.caveat: One week into Season M-6. This is the Salamence six to build from available evidence — not a claim of proven highest win rate.

stats.label: Salamencite
stats.note: Almost every ladder Salamence is the Mega.

stats.label: DD / DE / EQ / Roost
stats.note: Do not overcomplicate the first Salamence set.

stats.label: Golisopite
stats.note: Golisopod is basically always the Mega when brought as such.

stats.label: Lucarionite Z
stats.note: Timid Nasty Plot special is the concentrated ladder set.

construction.thesis: For a Salamence-centered M-C 3v3 six, build Mega Salamence + Primarina + Gholdengo, then hold Garchomp + Golisopod + Lucario as the three flex / alternate-Mega pieces.
construction.method: Start from Salamence's teammate cluster and the top-six ladder, then interpret roles — do not paste the five most common partners. Substitute Hippowdon → Gholdengo so the six gains Fairy resist, special offense, and Recover without stacking three Ground-oriented physical pieces next to Salamence and Garchomp.
construction.winCondition: Create one safe Dragon Dance on Mega Salamence, or switch Mega identity (Garchomp / Golisopod / Lucario) when their six makes Salamence the wrong stone.

substitutions.why: Hippowdon is #5 and legitimate, but Salamence + Garchomp + Hippowdon compress into the same physical/Ground defensive story. Gholdengo adds Steel/Ghost special pressure, Fairy resistance, Nasty Plot, Recover, and Air Balloon — things this six wants more than a second Sand wall.

altSlots.why: Excellent Salamence partner on teammate lists. Prefer Gholdengo here for a cleaner special-offensive complement; keep Aegislash as the first alternate sixth-slot candidate.

megaPool.rule: One Mega Evolution per battle. Register four stones; choose which stone after the 90-second preview.
megaPool.previewPressure: They see Salamence / Garchomp / Golisopod / Lucario and must guess which one actually Mega Evolves. That ambiguity is the point of the six.

candidates.when: Default. Physical-heavy foes, Intimidate value, and a clear Dragon Dance window.
Their six is Ground-vulnerable and Mega Salamence is awkward into their Fairy / Ice answers.
You need First Impression / Sucker Punch to deny free turns into fragile offense.
They are stacked for physical Mega Salamence; special Nasty Plot coverage cracks Fairy/Steel structures.

pilot.thesis: Salamence is the primary win condition when they lack a clean Flying answer — but the six wins by picking the right Mega and the right two supports, not by forcing the default three every game.
pilot.rule: Do not Mega until you know which stone answers their six. Do not bring three physical Ground-leaning names when Fairy is the hole.
pilot.fail: Auto-bring Salamence / Primarina / Gholdengo and auto-Mega Salamence into a six that hard-punishes Flying setup.

press: Force them to respect four possible Megas before the lead drops.
Encore setup and Protect turns with Primarina.
Split physical and special pressure so stacking Defense does not solve the six.
refuse: Never Mega two names — you only get one.
Never treat teammate frequency as a finished roster.
Never leave Salamence in on Fairy without Gholdengo or a plan.

plan.title: Preview
plan.goal: Name which of your four stones they fear most, and which support plugs their wincon.
plan.play: Mark Fairy, Ice, priority, and Ground-weak structures. Choose Mega and the three together.
plan.next: Lead the piece that denies their first free turn.

plan.title: Clock
plan.goal: Create the Dragon Dance window or the priority trade that opens it.
plan.play: Primarina Encores, Golisopod First Impressions, Gholdengo Recover-scouts — then Mega when the answer is gone.
plan.next: Clean with the remaining special or Ground pressure.

plan.title: Close
plan.goal: Finish without donating the Mega to a revenge killer.
plan.play: Roost or Recover to stay above revenge ranges. Lucario or Gholdengo clean if Salamence is chipped out.
plan.next: If the wrong Mega went down, next game change stone — not the whole six.

switches.send: Gholdengo — Steel resists Fairy; Make It Rain answers.
Salamence for Intimidate, or Golisopod to First Impression.
Garchomp Earthquake / Flamethrower or Lucario Aura Sphere.

victims.name: Physical Balance without Fairy
victims.why: Intimidate Mega + Primarina Encore + Gholdengo Recover outlast midrange.

victims.name: Glass HO
victims.why: Golisopod priority and Primarina Aqua Jet punish free turns.

victims.name: Defense-stacked physical cores
victims.why: Lucario / Gholdengo Nasty Plot lines ignore the physical wall.

counters.name: Multiple Fairy + Ice answers
counters.why: Salamence dance windows disappear — bring Lucario Mega or refuse the dance.

counters.name: Bulky Ground / Rock into Electric holes
counters.why: Gholdengo Balloon helps once; do not donate free entries.

counters.name: Fast special offense into Primarina
counters.why: Encore fails if you die first — lead Golisopod or Gholdengo instead.

advantages.title: Mega ambiguity
advantages.body: Four stones on preview force a wrong guess. Correct Mega choice is often more valuable than a perfect lead.
advantages.rule: Decide the stone with the three — not after the lead drops.

advantages.title: Physical / special split
advantages.body: Salamence and Golisopod punch; Gholdengo and Lucario plot. Opponents cannot solve the six with one defensive stack.
advantages.play: If they show Rocky Helmet / Assault Vest physical answers, lean special packs.

loops.title: Encore → Dance
loops.body: Primarina Encores a setup or Protect turn, then Salamence Dragon Dances into the free window.

loops.title: First Impression → handoff
loops.body: Golisopod deletes or chips the lead, U-turns into Salamence or Gholdengo with tempo.

loops.title: Plot race
loops.body: Gholdengo or Lucario Nasty Plots while Salamence threatens the physical dance — they cannot answer both cleanly.

hazards.title: Ice on the kite
hazards.body: Do not Dragon Dance into known Ice. Chip it with Primarina or Golisopod first.
hazards.watch: Choice Scarf Ice and priority Ice.

hazards.title: Fairy into Salamence
hazards.body: Gholdengo is the resist. Without it on the three, do not force the Mega Dance.
hazards.rule: No Fairy answer on the three → different pack.

roster.title: The Sky Hammer
roster.role: Primary physical setup win condition. Intimidate on entry, Mega when the Flying answer is gone, Dragon Dance once.
roster.itemWhy: Statistical center of M-C Salamence (~98% stone). Reserves the once-per-battle Mega for the matchup where Aerilate pressure matters most.

training.label: Standard DD
training.why: Mirror the ladder: max Attack and Speed with leftover HP. Adamant over Jolly until Speed tiers demand otherwise.
spend: 32 Spe — make Dragon Dance convert into a cleaner.

moves.name: Dragon Dance
moves.why: ~73% ladder. Converts Salamence from an attacker into the primary cleaner.

moves.name: Double-Edge
moves.why: ~76% ladder. Aerilate Flying STAB after Mega — the main damage button.

moves.name: Earthquake
moves.why: ~71% ladder. Punishes Steel, Rock, and Electric answers that resist Flying.

moves.name: Roost
moves.why: ~66% ladder. Recovers recoil so the endgame stays alive.

roster.objective: One safe Dragon Dance, then end the game.
roster.howToPlay:
Do not Mega automatically — Intimidate first when the physical lead matters.
Do not Dance while a faster Ice or Fairy revenge killer is healthy.
Double-Edge neutral targets; Earthquake the Steels.
Roost before you fall into revenge range.
If their six hard-punishes Flying, leave the stone on another Mega this game.

roster.title: The Encore Glue
roster.role: Fairy/Water balance piece. Punishes Dragons, Fire, and Ground; Encores setup and Protect turns so Salamence gets the window.
roster.itemWhy: Keeps Primarina in Encore and Aqua Jet range after chip — the glue needs to live.

training.label: Fast special
training.why: 32 SpA / 32 Spe with leftover HP matches the ladder pressure set.
spend: 32 SpA — Moonblast and Sparkling Aria damage.
32 Spe — outpace midrange Dragons and land Encore first.

moves.name: Moonblast
moves.why: Primary Fairy STAB — answers Dragons and threatens Salamence's Ice neighbors.

moves.name: Sparkling Aria
moves.why: Water STAB that spreads chip and can clear burns in relevant spots.

moves.name: Aqua Jet
moves.why: Priority finish on weakened targets when Golisopod is not on the three.

moves.name: Encore
moves.why: Punishes setup and Protect — creates the free turn Salamence wants.

roster.objective: Glue the matchup and create one Encore window for the Mega.
roster.howToPlay:
Lead or mid-game into Dragons and Fire.
Encore setup and Protect turns — do not waste it on locked Choice moves you already beat.
Aqua Jet weakened HO names.
Stay healthy enough that Sitrus keeps you in the game.

roster.title: The Fairy Net
roster.role: Special attacker and Fairy resist. The piece added instead of Hippowdon so the six is not all physical Ground pressure.
roster.itemWhy: ~65% ladder. Blocks the first Ground hit so Gholdengo can Plot or Make It Rain.

training.label: Plot special
training.why: Ladder set is extremely concentrated — max SpA and Spe with leftover HP.
spend: 32 SpA — Make It Rain / Shadow Ball damage.
32 Spe — outpace midrange after Nasty Plot.

moves.name: Make It Rain
moves.why: ~92% ladder. Steel STAB that answers Fairy and pressures Neutrals.

moves.name: Shadow Ball
moves.why: ~99% ladder. Ghost coverage into Fighting and Psychic.

moves.name: Nasty Plot
moves.why: ~84% ladder. Special setup path opponents cannot ignore while watching Salamence.

moves.name: Recover
moves.why: ~64% ladder. Longevity so the Fairy net stays on the board.

roster.objective: Absorb Fairy, force special answers, and Plot when they stack physical Defense.
roster.howToPlay:
Switch into Fairy aimed at Salamence.
Spend Balloon deliberately — the second Ground hits.
Nasty Plot when they cannot revenge cleanly.
Recover before you donate the net.

roster.title: The Other Mega
roster.role: Alternative Mega + Ground pressure + hazards. Preview ambiguity next to Salamence is half the value.
roster.itemWhy: ~35% of ladder Garchomp — the Mega share. On this six it is a deliberate second stone, not Scarf/Sash default.

itemAlts.name: Choice Scarf
itemAlts.why: If you decide Salamence is always the Mega this event, Scarf Chomp still revenge and pivot.

itemAlts.name: Focus Sash
itemAlts.why: Trade into Ice leads when hazards are already up elsewhere.

training.label: Fast Mega
training.why: Jolly max Attack / Speed so Mega Garchomp races midrange after the stone.

moves.name: Earthquake
moves.why: Primary Ground STAB — punishes Electric, Fire, Steel, Rock.

moves.name: Stealth Rock
moves.why: Chip Flying and Ice answers before Salamence dances.

moves.name: Dragon Tail
moves.why: Phaze setup and force switches into Rocks.

moves.name: Flamethrower
moves.why: Special coverage into Steel that walls Earthquake.

roster.objective: Be the Mega when Ground pressure beats Flying setup — or support Salamence with Rocks and phaze.
roster.howToPlay:
On preview, decide if Chomp or Salamence is the stone.
Lead Chomp into Ground-weak sixes.
Set Rocks before forcing the dance on Salamence games.
Do not donate into Ice without a plan.

roster.title: You Don't Get a Turn
roster.role: Immediate priority pressure. Salamence asks for a turn; Golisopod denies theirs.
roster.itemWhy: ~99% ladder — Golisopod is the Mega when the stone is registered. Tough Claws after Mega.

training.label: Bulky priority
training.why: 32 HP / 32 Atk keeps First Impression and Sucker Punch hitting while Emergency Exit still functions.
spend: 32 HP — live to Emergency Exit and keep priority relevant.
32 Atk — maximize First Impression / Iron Head / Sucker Punch.

moves.name: First Impression
moves.why: Opening priority — deletes weakened or frail leads in 3v3.

moves.name: Iron Head
moves.why: Steel STAB into Fairy and Ice after Mega Tough Claws.

moves.name: Sucker Punch
moves.why: Priority Dark into Psychic and Ghost revenge attempts.

moves.name: U-turn
moves.why: Hands Salamence or Gholdengo in safely after the chip.

roster.objective: Take the first turn of the game away from them, then hand off.
roster.howToPlay:
Lead when their six is fragile or HO-shaped.
First Impression the name you came for — do not soft-click.
U-turn into Salamence when Intimidate or Dance is ready.
Mega when Tough Claws Iron Head / Sucker Punch closes better than keeping Emergency Exit mid-game.

roster.title: The Special Blade
roster.role: Second setup sweeper on the special side. Stops opponents from solving the six with physical Defense.
roster.itemWhy: ~91% ladder. Timid Nasty Plot Mega is the concentrated special set.

training.label: Timid Plot
training.why: ~73% Timid on ladder — race after Nasty Plot with max SpA.
spend: 32 SpA — Aura Sphere / Flash Cannon / Dark Pulse.

moves.name: Nasty Plot
moves.why: ~80% ladder. The special dance that mirrors Salamence's physical Dance.

moves.name: Aura Sphere
moves.why: ~79% ladder. Never-miss Fighting into Normal, Rock, Steel, Ice.

moves.name: Flash Cannon
moves.why: ~75% ladder. Steel into Fairy.

moves.name: Dark Pulse
moves.why: ~74% ladder. Dark into Psychic and Ghost.

roster.objective: Be the Mega when Fairy/Steel structures invalidate physical Salamence.
roster.howToPlay:
Bring with Gholdengo when they look physically prepared.
Plot once the revenge killer is gone.
Aura Sphere the Neutrals; Flash Cannon the Fairies.
Do not lead Lucario into a known faster priority Dark or Ghost without Sash support from elsewhere.

slots.title: The Sky Hammer
slots.objective: One safe Dragon Dance, then end the game.

slots.title: The Fairy Net
slots.objective: Hold Fairy and Plot when needed.

packs.label: Default balance
packs.when: Their six is structurally midrange — no hard Flying wall stack, no pure HO glass that demands Golisopod first.
packs.identity: Salamence wincon, Primarina glue, Gholdengo Fairy net and special pressure.

strategy.opponentPattern: Balanced or mildly offensive six without a concentrated anti-Flying core.
strategy.purpose: Default teaching package — glue, Fairy resist, and the primary Mega Dance.
refuses: Pure HO that needs First Impression day one
strategy.winCondition: Encore or chip into one safe Dragon Dance on Mega Salamence.

pilot.thesis: Make them answer Salamence while Gholdengo holds Fairy and Primarina holds the turn.
pilot.rule: Mega Salamence only after the Flying answer is weakened or Encore'd.
pilot.fail: Dance on sight into Scarf Ice.

packs.philosophy: This is the starting three to learn — not a mandatory every-game bring.
refuse: Never leave Salamence in on Moonblast

plan.title: Glue
plan.play: Primarina and Gholdengo scout while chip accumulates.
plan.next: Dance when the answer is gone.

packs.label: Physical pressure
packs.when: They are Ground-vulnerable, Fairy pressure is light, and Garchomp gets immediate value.
packs.identity: Salamence + Garchomp Mega ambiguity with Primarina coverage.

strategy.opponentPattern: Electric / Fire / Steel-heavy structures that fear Ground, without a hard Fairy wall.
strategy.purpose: Force them to guess Salamencite vs Garchompite Z while Primarina handles Dragons and Ice.
refuses: Sand teams that invite Hippo wars you are not built for
strategy.winCondition: Rocks + phaze or Mega Ground pressure, with Dance as the backup wincon.

pilot.thesis: Pick the Mega that their six cannot answer — not the one you practiced more.
pilot.rule: If Fairy is light and Ground is free, Mega Chomp is legal.
pilot.fail: Mega both in your head and play neither correctly.

refuse: Ice leads without Primarina answer ready

packs.label: Anti-offense
packs.when: Their six is HO-shaped — glass, Sash, and early KOs.
packs.identity: Golisopod denies the turn; Primarina bulk + Aqua Jet; Salamence closes.

strategy.opponentPattern: Hyper Offense or fragile Balance that wins by taking free turns.
strategy.purpose: Survive the opening assault with priority and Encore, then convert to Salamence.
refuses: Fat Balance that walls First Impression
strategy.winCondition: First Impression chip into Intimidate / Dance or Aqua Jet cleanup.

pilot.thesis: You are not outspeeding everything — you are taking their first turn away.
pilot.rule: Lead Golisopod when the lead is frail.
pilot.fail: Leading Salamence into their Sash revenge chain.

press: First Impression the name you came for
refuse: Soft First Impression into a resist

packs.label: Special offense
packs.when: They are stacked for physical Mega Salamence — Assault Vest, Rocky Helmet, physical walls.
packs.identity: Two Nasty Plot paths plus Salamence Dance — three setup routes.

strategy.opponentPattern: Physically prepared sixes that look ready for Aerilate Double-Edge.
strategy.purpose: Force special answers while still threatening a physical Dance if they over-correct.
refuses: Fast special revenge with multiple priority Darks
strategy.winCondition: Nasty Plot on Lucario or Gholdengo, with Salamence as the cross-up.

pilot.thesis: If they solved physical Salamence in preview, do not give them that game.
pilot.rule: Plot only when revenge is gone.
pilot.fail: Mega Salamence into the wall they built for it.

packs.label: Maximum pressure
packs.when: You want to deny free turns and end the game before midrange chess starts.
packs.identity: Golisopod opens, Salamence mids, Lucario cleans — stop giving them turns.

strategy.opponentPattern: Sixes that lose to continuous offense and cannot afford a setup turn.
strategy.purpose: Most aggressive bring — priority into Dance into special Plot cleanup.
targets: Slow TR without Armor Tail answers
strategy.winCondition: Early chip → Mega Dance or Mega Lucario Plot while they are on the back foot.

pilot.thesis: Tempo over glue — accept less recovery for more pressure.
pilot.rule: Every turn should remove a threat or create a Dance/Plot window.
pilot.fail: Playing this like the default Primarina glue package.
